walkthroughs.body_html:
Beliefs about Deity — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Beliefs about Deity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Beliefs about Deity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: When was the Trinity affirmed by council?
options: AD 33
AD 325

mcqs.q: Who developed the doctrine of original sin?
options: Aquinas
Augustine
Luther
Calvin

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological argument try to prove?
options: That the existence of the universe requires a first cause or necessary being — usually identified with God — to explain why anything exists at all.
The cosmological argument proves the Big Bang happened.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The cosmological argument proves who created life on Earth.
